description: Snowflake's select-list rule under the super-group forms, all live-verified: GROUPING SETS / ROLLUP / CUBE apply the SAME check as a plain GROUP BY, with the UNION of every grouping set as the grouped keys. A column in ANY set is legal - its rows print NULL for the sets that aggregate it away - and a column in NONE is refused with the plain form's exact sentence, positioned at the offending REFERENCE's own line and 0-based column rather than at the select-list start. The rule reaches through a GROUPING() argument, which does not launder an ungrouped column, and a FROM alias spells the refusal's qualifier. A key written as a select ALIAS or a 1-based ORDINAL resolves to the aliased or numbered select expression, for validation and for execution alike. GROUPING SETS (()) groups by nothing at all, so a bare column has nowhere to hide. Converted 1:1 from query/GroupingSetsSelectListValidationTest (now retired); the six refusals keep the full message with its embedded newline, exactly as the Java's assertEquals did.

steps.sql: CREATE TABLE sales (region VARCHAR, product VARCHAR, amount NUMBER)
INSERT INTO sales VALUES ('east','a',10),('west','b',20)
SELECT region, product, SUM(amount) FROM sales GROUP BY GROUPING SETS ((product))

error.messageContains:
SQL compilation error: error line 1 at position 7
'SALES.REGION' in select clause is neither an aggregate nor in the group by clause.
